battle.name: 隋滅伊吾之戰
battle.brief: 大業四年（608年），隋煬帝以兵部尚書右衛大將軍薛世雄為敦煌道行軍元帥，率兵出敦煌討伊吾。精騎夜襲柳谷得手，追奔白水，進克伊吾城，俘其王，置伊吾郡。卡面兵器為古埃及月牙劍，形制早於本役三千餘年，其單刃外彎、砍下不需拔出的刀法，同西域彎刀最為相類。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 這場戰爭是隋朝大業四年（608年）在大漠西端對伊吾的一次軍事兼管轄行動。隋方主體是中原王朝的直轄軍：兵部尚書右衛大將軍薛世雄受命為敦煌道行軍元帥，率關中宿衛與沿邊徵發的兵馬自敦煌出發，兵員中既有禁軍宿衛，也有涼州、瓜州一線就地集中的邊兵，以及隨軍的輜重、馬匹、駱駝；資治通鑑記此役「發兵及西域諸國兵」，說明高昌、焉耆一類受隋朝冊封的附庸也以兵力或糧秣助戰。伊吾一方是聚居在今哈密綠洲的商胡勢力，隋書西域傳說其地「多商胡」，其王表面入朝貢玉，實際與西突厥往來密切，一旦有事就閉城自守；西突厥則以游騎控制天山北道與柳谷、白水一帶的商道要衝，藉伊吾卡住河西通往西域的門戶。第三方的角色並不單純：吐谷渾控制青海道，與西域往來不絕；鄯善、且末、龜茲等城邦多持觀望，隋廷正靠郡縣與使節兩手把它們逐步納入秩序。整場戰爭的本質，是隋朝要在絲路北道最窄的一段上，用一次成功的突擊換取永久的通道與站管權。
countriesEn: This war was a military and administrative operation carried out by the Sui dynasty at the western end of the great desert in the fourth year of the Daye era (608). The Sui side was built around the directly controlled forces of the central plain: Xue Shixiong, Minister of War and commander of the Right Guard, was appointed commander-in-chief of the Dunhuang route and marched out of Dunhuang with troops drawn from the palace guards of Guanzhong together with levies mustered along the frontier. His marching force included not only garrison soldiers but border troops concentrated locally around Liangzhou and Guazhou, together with baggage animals and draught animals; the Zizhi Tongjian records that the expedition "mustered troops and the soldiers of the states of the Western Regions", meaning that client states under Sui investiture such as Gaochang and Yanqi contributed men or provisions. The Yiwu side was the merchant communities of the Hami oasis in present-day Xinjiang; the Sui Shu, in its treatise on the Western Regions, states that the land abounded in merchants and foreigners, and that its ruler nominally came to court and offered jade while in fact keeping close contact with the Western Turks, and whenever trouble came the city simply shut its gates and held out. The Western Turks in turn used mounted patrols to control the trade road along the northern Tian Shan around Liugu and Baishui, using Yiwu to close the gate that led from Hexi into the Western Regions. The role of third parties was not simple: the Tuyuhun held the Qinghai route and never stopped contacting the oasis states, and cities such as Shanshan, Qiemo and Kucha watched from the side, drawn into the Sui order by a combination of commanderies and envoys. At bottom, this campaign was an attempt to win one decisive surprise attack on the narrowest stretch of the northern silk road, and to convert it into a permanent corridor and a permanent seat of Sui administration.
people: 隋煬帝楊廣是這場戰爭的發起者。大業四年二月，朝廷下詔以兵部尚書右衛大將軍薛世雄為敦煌道行軍元帥，討伊吾；這道詔令背後的西域布局，由祕書監裴矩的經營鋪墊：裴矩早年奉命安撫西域，輾轉取得西域山川形勢與諸國風土人情，撰成《西域圖記》供行軍參考，並在河西一線推動屯田積穀、編排商旅護送，使敦煌與張掖成為西征的糧秣與情報節點。主帥薛世雄是關西老將，久歷軍旅，奉命後即在敦煌整軍、偵察伊吾與突厥游騎的集結位置，選銳騎夜襲柳谷，追奔白水，再進圖伊吾城，戰罷還師奏捷。伊吾方面，漢代以來即設城置校的伊吾盧此時由商胡首領控制，其王在城破之後被俘，隨軍送京師，諸部首領亦隨之就擒；城中商胡百姓則依例被編為郡縣屬民，繼續受隋朝在城內所設校尉的管束。史書對此役的個人記載其實相當稀薄，除了上述詔令、將帥與被俘的首領群體，具名者甚少；這種寫法本身就說明西域遠征在隋廷的檔案裡只是一件以軍功結案的邊事。
peopleEn: Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, was the man who set the campaign in motion. In the second month of the fourth year of Daye he issued the edict appointing Xue Shixiong, Minister of War and commander of the Right Guard, as commander-in-chief of the Dunhuang route to punish Yiwu. The strategic background behind that edict had been prepared by Pei Ju, Keeper of the Secret Archive, who had earlier been sent to pacify the Western Regions, gathered detailed knowledge of their mountains, rivers, customs and manners, and compiled the Record of the Western Regions for the use of marching armies; Pei Ju also pushed farming settlements and grain stores along the Hexi corridor and organized armed escort for merchants, so that Dunhuang and Zhangye became the supply and intelligence nodes of the western expedition. The commander, Xue Shixiong, was an experienced frontier officer from Guanzhong; once the order came he mustered and drilled his men at Dunhuang, reconnoitred where the Yiwu and Turkic horsemen were concentrating, then led picked cavalry in a night attack at Liugu, pursued the enemy to Baishui, and finally assaulted the city of Yiwu before returning to court to report the victory. On the Yiwu side, the place that had been an official city with a commandant since Han times, the walled post of Yiwu Lu, was then controlled by merchant chieftains; after the city fell, the king was taken captive and sent to the capital with the army, and the local leaders came in with him. The people of the town, merchants included, were enrolled as the population of the new commandery and remained under the commandant installed there. The record of the war is in fact very thin on individuals: apart from the edict, the general, the captive king and the group of chiefs, almost no personal names survive, and that silence itself shows how the campaign was filed away in the Sui archives as a piece of frontier business closed on the strength of a single military merit.
kits: 卡面這件兵器是埃及月牙劍（Khopesh），青銅時代的產物，約成形於公元前一千五百年上下，刃身向外彎曲如新月，單面開鋒，握柄有時穿孔或加縛以便雙手握持；它最出名的特性是砍下去不必拔出——彎曲的刃在斬中之後會帶住目標，騎士或士兵順勢往下拖拽即可切開肌肉與筋腱，而不必像直刃那樣先把刀拔出來再揮第二下。這套力學在六百零八年的伊吾城下早已不存在同型武器：按隋朝與西域的兵器序列，漢地軍隊裝備的是環首刀一類的直刃環柄刀，配合步槊、長矛與兩手執握的刀，騎兵多佩刀與長槊；西域與突厥的戰士則用源自波斯—粟特系統的鐮刀型彎刀，同樣是單刃外彎、以砍擊與拖割為主，殺傷邏輯與月牙劍最為接近。攻城一方則是雲梯、巢車、撞車與投石機一類器械，隋書禮志所載的火獸、火鵝等燃燒破壞裝置亦在守城與攻城器之列；後勤方面則依賴駱駝、馬匹、輜重車，以及敦煌、張掖屯田所積與隨軍攜帶的糧水。以單刃、彎曲、咬住不放的刀身，對付尚未被攻破的城牆與密集的守軍，正是本卡兵器在它的原生年代所擅長的場合。
kitsEn: The weapon on the card is the Egyptian khopesh, a product of the Bronze Age that took shape around 1500 BC. Its blade curves outward like a new moon, it is sharpened on a single edge, and the grip is sometimes pierced or bound for a two-handed hold. Its most famous property is that it does not have to be pulled free after the blow: the curved blade catches in what it cuts, so a rider or foot soldier simply drags it downward to open muscle and sever tendons, instead of having to wrench the blade out and swing again. No weapon of that type existed at the gates of Yiwu in 608. In the arms inventories of the Sui and of the oasis peoples, the Chinese field armies carried straight single-edged swords with ring pommels, used together with long spears and two-handed swords, while cavalry carried the sword and the long lance; the warriors of the oasis and of the Turks used the sickle-shaped sabre that came out of the Persian-Sogdian system, likewise single-edged and outcurved, worked mainly by cutting and dragging, and its killing logic is the closest to that of the khopesh. On the besieging side the equipment was the assault ladder, the wheeled siege tower, the battering ram and the traction trebuchet; the Sui Shu in its chapter on ritual also lists burning devices such as the fire beast and the fire goose among the offensive and defensive machines. On the logistics side the expedition depended on camels, horses, baggage carts, and on grain raised in the farming settlements of Dunhuang and Zhangye and carried with the column. Cutting with a single-edged, outcurved blade that catches and does not need to be withdrawn was exactly the task the card's weapon was built for in its own age, and exactly the task a blade like that faced when it was used against a city wall that had not yet been breached and a dense body of defenders.
tactics: 這場戰役的樣板是一整套沙漠邊境上的突擊加接管。隋軍自敦煌出發，沿疏勒河谷這條唯一有水的通道西行，一路上以綠洲驛站為依托。人馬一到伊吾地界，先不急著攻城，而是分遣斥候與歸附的商胡嚮導，探明西突厥游騎的營位與巡邏路線；確認敵情後選擇無月之夜，以精騎為先鋒，離營急行，插入柳谷一帶的谷口，這就是史書記載的夜擊胡人於柳谷。天明之後，隋軍藉地勢與騎兵衝擊的餘勢壓住潰退的敵騎，緊追不捨，把戰場推到白水一線，逼得突厥部眾退保既有的水源與城障。攻城階段，隋軍分兩路：一隊封鎖城外的田地、水渠與商隊通道，斷絕城內的柴草與糧食；一隊列陣攻城，步兵在弩手與長槊掩護下把雲梯、撞車推近城牆，騎兵在兩翼等待破城後追擊潰兵。城破之後，隋軍沒有就地長久逗留：先封存城中的武器與糧食，收編降卒與被裹挾的商旅，然後在城內設郡置尉，把原來依附突厥的商胡首領體系拆散，改編為隋朝在西域的屬民與吏員。整個過程的節奏是：偵察、夜襲、追擊、圍城、打通驛道、留下守軍與官署。
tacticsEn: The pattern of this war was a complete sequence of surprise attack and takeover along a desert frontier. The Sui column left Dunhuang and moved west along the Shule river valley, the single corridor that carried water, using the oasis stations as its line of support. On reaching Yiwu territory they did not rush the walls: they sent out scouts and guides drawn from the merchant communities to find out where the Turkic horsemen had camped and how they patrolled, and once the enemy was located they chose a moonless night, put picked cavalry in front, marched out of camp in haste and slipped into the mouth of the valley at Liugu, which is the night attack on the foreigners at Liugu that the histories record. At daybreak the Sui force used the momentum of the charge and the advantage of the ground to break the fleeing riders, pursued without halt, and pushed the fighting back to the line of Baishui, where the Turkic riders were driven to shelter around their own water and their existing works. For the siege the Sui army split in two: one detachment sealed the fields, canals and caravan tracks outside the city to cut off firewood and grain from within, while the other formed up to attack, infantry and lancers covered by crossbowmen pushing ladders and rams against the walls, with cavalry waiting on the flanks to chase the fugitives once the city fell. After the breach the army did not linger: the weapons and stores in the city were secured, the surrendered soldiers and the merchants swept up in the fighting were enrolled, and the chief system that had hung on the Turks was broken up inside the walls and turned into the subjects and officials of a Sui commandery in the West. The rhythm of the whole operation was reconnaissance, night attack, pursuit, encirclement, breach, opening of the post road, and the stationing of a garrison with its offices.
data: 可核對的數字並不多，這場戰爭的記載本來就以定性描述為主。時間上，詔令下於隋煬帝大業四年（608年）二月，主力自敦煌出發，戰鬥集中在同年三、四月；隔年大業五年（609年），隋煬帝西巡至張掖，會西域二十七國來朝的使者，於河西與西域一線新置西海、河源、鄯善、且末、伊吾五郡。地理上，敦煌至伊吾沿古道約一千二百里上下，按當時步騎日行數十里計，單程約需三旬；柳谷、白水、伊吾城同在這條線上，實際交鋒發生在伊吾城東北方向的綠洲與戈壁交錯地帶。兵員方面，史文只說「發兵及西域諸國兵」，未載確數，一般推想為數萬之眾，其中能夜行疾馳的精騎是出奇制勝的主力，步卒與器械兵在攻城中居次。器械數量、攻城日程與俘虜總數，隋書與資治通鑑都沒有留下可靠記載，只能說隋軍在敦煌的整備與屯田積穀至少供應了一支遠征軍隊所需的糧秣與馬匹，而被俘的伊吾王及諸首領是史書唯一明確記下姓名的收穫。兵器的形制可以量化：月牙劍屬青銅時代的短刀，長度與現代單刃匕首相當，遠不能與隋朝鍛造的環首刀相比，但同屬單刃刀類；本役真正被記錄下來的距離，是從敦煌到伊吾的一段，而它的長度，後來變成唐朝通往西域的驛路。
dataEn: Few numbers survive, and that is the nature of the record: this campaign is described mainly in qualitative terms. In time, the edict was issued in the second month of the fourth year of Daye (608); the main force marched out of Dunhuang and the fighting fell in the third and fourth months of the same year. In the following year, in the fifth year of Daye (609), Emperor Yang of Sui toured the west as far as Zhangye, received envoys from twenty-seven states of the Western Regions, and set up five new commanderies along the Hexi and western roads: Xihai, Heyuan, Shanshan, Qiemo and Yiwu. Geographically the old road from Dunhuang to Yiwu runs roughly twelve hundred li, and at the thirty or forty li a day that foot and horse columns of the period could manage, the journey in one direction took about three tens of days. Liugu, Baishui and the city of Yiwu all lie on that line, and the actual clash took place on the belt of oasis and gravel northeast of the city. On strength the histories say only that the expedition mustered troops and the soldiers of the states of the Western Regions, without a figure; it is generally taken to have been a force of several tens of thousands, with the cavalry able to ride fast by night forming the spear of the surprise, and the foot and machine crews taking a secondary part in the siege. Numbers of machines, the length of the siege, and the total of the captives are not reliably preserved in either the Sui Shu or the Zizhi Tongjian; all that can be said is that the preparations at Dunhuang, including the grain from the farming settlements, fed the supplies and horses of an expeditionary column, and that the captured king of Yiwu and his chiefs are the only results the histories name individually. The weapon shapes can be quantified: the khopesh is a Bronze Age short sword, comparable in length to a modern single-edged dagger and no match for the forged ring-pommel swords of the Sui, though both belong to the single-edged sword family. The one distance the record really preserves is the run from Dunhuang to Yiwu, and that stretch of road later became the post road of the Tang into the Western Regions.
cause: 打起來的原因有遠有近。遠因是絲路北道的戰略地理：伊吾扼在敦煌與西域之間的咽喉，漢代以來就設伊吾盧城，隋朝也在此派官置校，商胡聚居、馬隊往來，是絲路北道上唯一同時具備水源與草場的樞紐；誰控制伊吾，誰就控制河西與西域之間的往來節奏。近因是伊吾的遊離：其王在名義上向隋朝入朝貢玉，實際上在隋文帝死後、隋煬帝忙於應付吐谷渾與高句麗的那幾年裡，與西突厥的往來重新加密，閉城自守、不聽隋朝節制，隋廷在敦煌的官署也屢次失去對當地的實際控制。制度上，裴矩在河西設計的方案是一整套的：屯田積穀以備兵資，編排護商以通有無，再配合郡縣與都護府把西域的城邦納入中原的編制，這條路要求先有一個守得住的支點，伊吾正是那個支點。於是每一次邊境報急，都會被理解為必須出手的理由。個人層面上，隋煬帝即位後要藉一場對外勝利立威，也藉此為進一步的西巡與更大的西域計劃鋪路，於是原本可以拖延的邊務被推成必須在一年內解決的戰役。
causeEn: The reasons run both deep and near. The deep reason is the strategic geography of the northern silk road: Yiwu sits at the throat between Dunhuang and the Western Regions. It had been the walled post of Yiwu Lu since Han times, the Sui kept officials and a commandant there, merchants and foreigners crowded together, and it was the one place on that road with water and pasture. Whoever held Yiwu held the rhythm of travel between Hexi and the West. The near reason was the drift of Yiwu itself: while its ruler nominally came to court and offered jade, in the years after Emperor Wen died, while Emperor Yang was absorbed by the Tuyuhun and Goguryeo, contacts with the Western Turks grew dense again; the city closed its gates, refused Sui control, and the Sui offices at Dunhuang lost effective hold on the region more than once. Institutionally, the plan Pei Ju had built along Hexi was a whole system: farming settlements to stock grain for war, escorted convoys to keep the road open, and commanderies and protectorates to fold the oasis states into the central order; such a scheme needed one foothold that could actually be held, and Yiwu was to be that foothold. Every report of trouble on the frontier could therefore be read as a reason to act. At the personal level, the new emperor wanted a foreign victory to establish his authority, and wanted it as the prelude to a grander tour of the West and a larger western plan, so a frontier business that might have been deferred was pushed into something that had to be settled within a single year.
impact: 這場戰役的直接後果，是隋朝在今哈密一帶拿到了第一個能自己守住的西域立足點。次年大業五年，隋煬帝親自西巡，抵達張掖，會見西域二十七國來朝的使者，並在河西至西域一線連設西海、河源、鄯善、且末、伊吾五郡，把中原王朝的郡縣建制第一次推過玉門關，敦煌到伊吾的驛道成為官道。行政與軍事的配套隨之落地：伊吾郡置校尉鎮守，屯田與護商在敦煌、張掖運作，絲路北道上的商旅活動因此在隋唐之際相對安全；敦煌這座原本只是軍鎮與驛站的城，也因為郡治與商貿的集中而成長為河西西部的重鎮。制度上的樣板同樣被後世沿用：唐太宗貞觀十四年滅高昌、設西州與安西都護府，其交通線、屯田與城防安排，都建立在隋朝這一輪經營之上；西域的羈縻州縣與都護府體系，於是由隋入唐，成為漢地王朝治理西域的常制。另一面，代價也在累積：為維持西域的郡縣與守軍，隋廷不得不在敦煌與河西長期屯兵積粟，而同一時期發動的高句麗戰爭又把大批丁役與物資抽調東去，遠征的開支與東征的消耗疊在一起，成為隋末局勢崩解的遠因之一。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was that the Sui gained its first foothold in the West it could hold on its own, in the oasis around present-day Hami. The next year, in the fifth year of Daye (609), Emperor Yang of Sui toured the west in person, reached Zhangye, met the envoys of twenty-seven states of the Western Regions, and established five commanderies in a row along Hexi and the western road: Xihai, Heyuan, Shanshan, Qiemo and Yiwu. For the first time the commandery-and-county system of the central plain was carried past the Jade Gate, and the road from Dunhuang to Yiwu became an official post road. The administrative and military apparatus followed: a commandant and a garrison were set at Yiwu, farming settlements and escorted trade operated from Dunhuang and Zhangye, and merchant traffic on the northern silk road was correspondingly secure around the Sui-Tang transition; Dunhuang, which had been little more than a garrison and a relay station, grew into a major town of western Hexi as the seat of a commandery and the center of trade. The institutional model was inherited in turn: when Taizong destroyed Gaochang in the fourteenth year of Zhenguan (640) and set up Xizhou and the Anxi Protectorate, its lines of communication, its farming settlements and its city defenses all stood on the foundations laid by this Sui round, and the system of frontier commanderies and protectorates through which the Chinese dynasties governed the West passed from Sui to Tang as a standing arrangement. The cost, meanwhile, accumulated. Keeping commanderies and garrisons in the West meant the Sui had to station troops and store grain at Dunhuang and along Hexi without end, and the war against Goguryeo drew men and supplies eastward at the same time; the outlays of the distant expedition and the drain of the eastern war were piled on top of one another, and became one of the distant causes of the collapse of the Sui order.
result: 打完了。薛世雄的精騎在柳谷夜襲得手，突厥游騎潰散，追奔到白水之後，隋軍進逼伊吾城；守軍抵抗數日，終以城破被攻下。伊吾王與諸部首領被俘，隨軍送往京師，隋朝在城內設伊吾郡、置校尉與守軍，把這個原來依附西突厥的商胡聚居點，改造成中原王朝在西域的前哨。降附的商胡百姓與被裹挾的商旅被重新編組，繼續在郡縣體系之下生活與貿易，絲路北道的水源、草場與驛站第一次被置於一位中國郡兵的直接管轄之下。消息傳開後，西域諸國的反應明顯分化：靠近伊吾的幾個小國震懾而趨於恭順，高昌、焉耆等則更積極地靠向隋廷；大業七年（611年），裴矩奉命再度出使西域、分化鐵勒部，並乘勢打擊西突厥，使隋朝在西域的優勢又延續了數年。然而結論要留半句：這是打開通道的勝利，不是解決問題的勝利。隋朝在西域的統治始終建立在不斷派兵、不斷屯田、不斷犒賞的開支上，一旦中原出現內亂，郡縣與守軍都會在幾年之內被放棄；唐人接手之後要重新做一遍，歷史才真正把這條通道固定下來。
resultEn: The fighting was done. Xue Shixiong's picked cavalry struck at night at Liugu, the Turkic riders broke, the pursuit carried them to Baishui, and the Sui army closed on the city of Yiwu; the defenders held for several days and were finally taken by assault. The king of Yiwu and the chiefs of the tribes were captured and sent to the capital with the army, and the Sui set up the prefecture of Yiwu inside the walls, with a commandant and a garrison, turning a merchant settlement that had hung on the Western Turks into an outpost of the central plain in the West. The surrendered population, merchants among them, was re-enrolled and went on living and trading under the commandery, and for the first time the water, the pasture and the relay stations of the northern road stood under the direct command of a Chinese garrison officer. The news carried well beyond the oasis: the small states near Yiwu were frightened into greater obedience, while Gaochang, Yanqi and others drew closer to the Sui court; in the seventh year of Daye (611) Pei Ju was sent to the Western Regions again, split the Tiele peoples away from the Turks, and struck at the Western Turks in their turn, so that the Sui advantage in the West lasted a few years longer. The conclusion needs half a sentence of qualification: this was a victory that opened a corridor, not one that solved a problem. Sui rule in the West rested on endless garrisons, endless stored grain and endless payments, and the moment disorder broke out in the central plain the commanderies and the soldiers were abandoned within a few years; the Tang had to take the work up again before the road was really fixed in place.
